title: search --json reports complete: true for the last reconcile, not the tree, when a daemon is watching
body:
`intent search --json` reports `"index": {"complete": true, ...}` with the `reconciled_at` of the last whole reconcile, even when a daemon is watching the project and the plain search skipped its own reconcile (issue 0443 Q1). `complete` is then a claim about the index as of that reconcile, not about the tree, so a caller cannot tell a complete answer from one the watcher has not yet caught up on. Driven on 3.1.0 under an isolated HOME: with `intentd` watching, a file written just before the search was missing from the hits while the envelope said `complete: true`. With the daemon stopped, the same search reconciled and found it.

The property is recorded in docs/known-defects.md ("The search index"). What the envelope should say instead is open: a field naming that the answer came from a watched index without a reconcile, a `complete` that is false while the watcher has unprocessed events, or a statement that `complete` never covers edits since `reconciled_at`.

Filed on vc's ruling, 2026-09-19.
